text:
THE FLOORS DECIDE A CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION QUESTION AND ARE DERIVED FROM A SAME-IMPLEMENTATION MEASUREMENT, AND THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. Raised by snorkeltoast 2026-09-10 against their own instrument, unprompted, in the same message that reported the first FAIL. **The per-slide floors come from a control that renders ONE artifact repeatedly and measures how much its own output moves** -- which is why most of them read 0.000000. That is the REFERENCE'S STABILITY. **What the compare actually asks is whether TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS agree**, and a floor of zero demands bit-exactness that no cross-language port can deliver on a lossy format: two conformant JPEG encoders at the same quality produce different bytes by construction, as AC-3.15 measured.
SO A ZERO FLOOR IS NOT A STRICT BAR, IT IS THE WRONG BAR, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS. It does not merely over-report; **it reports a difference that CANNOT be eliminated as though it were a defect that could**, which makes every FAIL uninformative in the same way a control with an empty population makes every PASS uninformative. A bar nothing can clear grades nothing.
THE FAIL SURVIVES THE CORRECTION AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ROW RATHER THAN A RETRACTION. All six slides over floor also exceed `min_defect` 0.223607, the declared noise floor, by between 4x and 13x. **AC-3.15's divergence is real under any sane bar**, so nothing about that finding rests on this defect -- which is exactly the shape that makes the defect easy to leave unfixed.
IT IS NOT AC-2.3, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. AC-2.3 governs whether stability decides GRADEABILITY, the flat repeat count of thirteen, and deriving a ceiling rather than taking a largest-observed value. **All of that is about ONE implementation and is correct.** This row is about what the resulting number is then USED TO DECIDE. Same instrument, different question, and AC-2.3 closing does not close this.
DISCHARGED WHEN THE FLOOR A CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION COMPARE GRADES AGAINST IS DERIVED FROM SOMETHING THAT COULD DISTINGUISH THE TWO CASES -- not when a number is raised. **snorkeltoast owns the derivation and vc will not prescribe its shape**; what this row refuses is a bar whose value came from measuring one implementation against itself. **The obvious repair -- fall back to `min_defect` for cross-implementation runs -- is ONE candidate and is not ruled in here**, because a single declared noise floor across every slide discards the per-slide structure AC-2.3 paid thirty captures to establish.

state.reason: CULLED 2026-09-11 by hv: instrument correctness on which no shipped outcome depends. The finding is true (floors measure the reference's self-stability, the compare asks cross-implementation agreement) and it changes nothing: all six divergent slides clear min_defect 0.223607 by 4x-13x, so AC-3.15's FAIL and hv's acceptance of the encoder divergence stand with or without it. The harness is snorkeltoast's instrument in snorkeltoast's repo; if they re-derive the floors that is their call and needs no Utilz row. Recorded in design.md section 0 as a known limit of the harness.
